AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 6, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with Norwalk
  City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 7011-00-9037, 8015-03-9020, 8024-01-9008, 8047-00-4022,
  8048-01-1035, 8052-00-9032, 8054-00-4011, 8056-01-8036, 8079-03-2019, and 8080-02-4012;
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating Party: County of Los
  Angeles Tax Assessor; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Rick Cartagena
  Grace Brethren Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Ericka Huape
  Santa Fe High School

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

  II.  City Council to recognize staff for their accomplishments in maintaining effective partnerships to serve
  the individual needs of homeless in Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to recognize staff and community partners for their success in enhancing the image and
  pride of our neighborhood through the Mini Mr. Sun and Property Enhancement programs.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Daily Luncheon Program Ribbon Cutting.

  2.  City Council to recognize the Norwalk Transportation Department’s 45th Anniversary.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT
   July 23, July 30, and August 6, 2019

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of July 16,
  July 23, and July 30, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve payroll for the periods of June 16, 2019 – June
  29, 2019, in the amount of $1,015,607.11 and June 30, 2019 – July 13, 2019, in the amount of
  $990,851.79. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period July
  10 - July 30, 2019, in the total amount of $4,063,514.90. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Jesus Jimenez
  and Griselda Mendoza. 830-10/13

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JULY 24, 2019 - No action is required unless the City Council
  elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the Commission’s
  action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-44 – DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 19-44, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE FINANCE
  DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT FOR COMMUNITY HOUSING DEVELOPMENT ORGANIZATION - Staff recommends
  City Council authorize the City Manager to execute all necessary agreements with Home Ownership
  for Personal Empowerment, Inc. to provide a Community Housing Development Organization project in
  the amount of $265,229 in HOME funds, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney.315-02-01

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-46 - STATE OF GOOD REPAIR PROGRAM AND ADDITIONAL STATE
  TRANSIT ASSISTANCE, AND AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 BUDGET - Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-46, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK SUPPORTING THE ALLOCATION REQUEST FOR THE SENATE BILL 1 CALIFORNIA
  STATE OF GOOD REPAIR PROGRAM, AND ADDITIONAL STATE TRANSIT ASSISTANCE, AND
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 BUDGET, in the amount of $145,114. 1105-02

  Report

  9.  AMENDMENT NO. 4 - WASTE MANAGEMENT (WM) CURBSIDE LLC AGREEMENT FOR
  RESIDENTIAL USED MOTOR OIL COLLECTION PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 4 with WM Curbside LLC for Used Oil Collection Program services, in an
  amount not to exceed $38,600 per year through June 30, 2020; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1065-04-01
   Report

  10. CONFIRM EMERGENCY REPAIR WORK – 11846 AND 12042 166th STREET, AND 14119
  CROSSDALE AVENUE - Staff recommends City Council confirm emergency repair work for three
  locations completed by Precision Pipeline, Inc., in the amount of $11,627.18.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  12. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1003
  AND PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 1996 – RESOLUTION NO. 19-47 APPROVING
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1003 AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-48 APPROVING PRECISE
  DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 1996 – 12177 AND 12182-12186 FRONT STREET - Staff recommends
  City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-47, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE APPROVAL OF
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1003; and

  b.  Resolution No. 19-48, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION RELATIVE TO THE APPROVAL OF
  PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 1996. 320-01-1003/320-04-1996

  Report

REPORT

  13. AGREEMENT - PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION OF NORWALK TRANSIT SYSTEM?S
  MICROTRANSIT PILOT PROGRAM AND OTHER MICRO-MOBILITY PROGRAMS - Staff
  recommends City Council approve an agreement with Judith Norman in the amount of $55,000 for
  planning and implementation of Norwalk Transit System’s Microtransit Pilot Program; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget,
  on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1120-12

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated August 2, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
